# Chapter code library {#sec-chapter-code}

These completed files bring together the code developed in the book. Use the descriptions to find a starting point for your own analysis, and follow the section links in parentheses to learn how each part works. The files use the example datasets from the chapters; adapt the data sources and analytical choices to suit your own project.

Save an R script in the `R` folder of your crime mapping workspace and open it in Positron. Save the Quarto report as `chapter_11.qmd` in your workspace, following @sec-reports. Before running a file, follow its chapter's instructions for installing packages and creating the required folders, including `data/raw`, `data/processed` and `output` where needed (@sec-create-project). The corrected `chapter_08.R` also needs the Bronx shootings and precinct files downloaded in @sec-creating-storing-map.

You can find finished example reports and reusable templates in @sec-resources. The Medellín report below is the same source file linked from that appendix, downloaded here with the filename used in @sec-reports.
